justification: Property-alerts delivery layer: a scheduled dispatcher emails subscribers about new development applications near their address, plus a token unsubscribe endpoint and a STOP-and-ask migration. No compliance/legal claims; email copy is factual listings verbatim from the NSW Planning Portal feeds. Standard tier because the dispatcher advances persisted dedup state and sends external email — the risk is silent-drop (marking items seen without a delivered email), covered by break-it tests.

pre_impl.existing_data: threat_radar_subscriptions (10 columns, 2 active rows live-introspected 2026-07-07) plus the subscribe/check helpers in services/threat_radar.py (_fetch_das, _filter_nearby, _get_conn) — reused, not duplicated. No email-dispatch or unsubscribe capability existed anywhere (the resend npm dep has zero usages).
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The table already has last_checked (not last_checked_at); the dispatcher uses the existing column. It was MISSING unsubscribe_token / consented_at / last_notified_at — added by the STOP-and-ask migration (not yet run). ePlanning payload shape captured from a live call (PlanningPortalApplicationNumber, ApplicationType, ApplicationStatus, LodgementDate, Location[0].FullAddress).
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: prior-art audited 2026-07-07: dispatcher reuses threat_radar helpers plus run_monitors conventions; unsubscribe extends the same router module; opt-in component mirrors PostResultEmailStrip and posts to the existing /api/satellite/threat-radar route.

functions.name: build_alert_email
functions.input: subscription row plus a list of new application dicts and the unsubscribe URL
functions.output: dict of subject, html and text — every application value rendered verbatim, missing values shown as an em dash, never fabricated
functions.if_none: an empty items list is never passed here (dispatch skips send when there are no new items); a golden fixture test pins the rendered output

functions.name: dispatch
functions.input: dry_run flag plus env (DATABASE_URL, RESEND_API_KEY); reads active subscriptions and the live ePlanning feeds
functions.output: exit 0 clean, exit 2 per-subscription failures (Telegram alerted), exit 1 run-level failure (no key, missing migration columns)
functions.if_none: no active subscriptions yields a clean exit 0 with a zero-count summary line

functions.name: unsubscribe
functions.input: unsubscribe_token query parameter (token only, no email — enumeration guard)
functions.output: sets active=false and returns a confirmation; idempotent on repeat clicks
functions.if_none: unknown token returns 404; empty or over-100-char token returns 422 before any DB call

values.value: application field values rendered into the email (number, type, status, lodgement date, distance, site address)
values.nullable: yes — _val returns an em dash for None or empty string, so a missing API field never becomes a blank or an invented value
values.if_missing: an absent or empty API field renders as an em dash (—), never a blank cell or a fabricated default; a test asserts this when Type/Status/Lodged are missing
values.guard_at: scripts/run_alerts_dispatch.py:85 (_val) plus a test asserting the em dash appears when Type/Status/Lodged are absent

queries.purpose: advance dedup state only after a confirmed 2xx send (the silent-drop guard)
queries.file_line: scripts/run_alerts_dispatch.py:218 (mark_notified), called at :292 only inside the send_resend success branch
queries.where_clause: WHERE id=%s — single subscription; seen_application_numbers merged via jsonb_build_object
queries.if_zero: a failed send skips mark_notified entirely, so the applications stay unseen and re-send on the next run rather than vanishing

queries.where_clause: WHERE unsubscribe_token=%s RETURNING id — token-only, no email; UPDATE matches regardless of current active value so repeat clicks are idempotent
queries.if_zero: no row means an unknown token, returned as 404 (a known-but-already-unsubscribed token still matches and returns a row)

break_it.scenario: Resend outage mid-run (send returns non-2xx or raises)
break_it.what_happens: mark_notified is not called, so dedup state is not advanced; the items re-send next run and the run exits 2 with a Telegram summary
break_it.how: send only advances state inside the truthy branch of send_resend; send_resend returns False on any non-2xx or exception

break_it.scenario: Both NSW ePlanning endpoints down (api_ok False)
break_it.what_happens: no send attempt and no state update at all — last_checked is not stamped so the next run retries, identical to the existing check() semantics
break_it.how: the api_ok guard continues the loop before filtering or sending

break_it.scenario: OnlineDA field rename/format change makes a value missing
break_it.what_happens: the affected cell renders an em dash rather than a fabricated value; per-subscription isolation contains any parse error to one subscriber
break_it.how: _val treats None/empty as absent; the send loop wraps each subscription in try/except and counts failures without aborting the run

break_it.scenario: Subscriber clicks the unsubscribe link twice, or an attacker guesses tokens
break_it.what_happens: the second click returns the same confirmation (idempotent); an unknown token is a 404 and the endpoint takes no email parameter so it cannot confirm whether an address is subscribed
break_it.how: token-only UPDATE ... RETURNING id; length guard rejects oversized tokens pre-DB

post_merge.secrets: Yes — RESEND_API_KEY must be added to the Railway property-alerts service (it lives in Vercel env for the frontend, not on the monitors service); the from: sending domain plotdetect.com.au must be verified in Resend
post_merge.manual_verify: Yes — apply migrations/add_property_alerts_columns.sql (STOP-and-ask, presented to user), then run scripts/run_alerts_dispatch.py --dry-run and read the output, then one real send to the founder address at a busy address (Marrickville), confirm the email renders and the unsubscribe link deactivates; verify the Railway service deploys and the cron fires once manually before trusting the schedule
